events.title: An Evening with Author David Slayton
events.description: Join us for a conversation, Q&A, and book signing with author David Slayton. David will be presenting Backwoods Banshee , book 5 in The Adam Binder Novels . About the Book As Adam copes with fresh trauma, he must investigate how Banshees are getting into our world, and who is trying to erase history from the books … Adam, Vic, and their friends are attending a concert, enjoying a rare moment of peace, when a man suddenly rushes the stage and screams, killing the musician and rendering many of the audience members unconscious. Adam quickly learns this is a banshee which has somehow slipped into this world from The Between, a realm outside of everything. While Adam tries to solve one mystery, the tension builds between him and his boyfriend, Vic, as Adam struggles to heal from the torture he suffered at the hands of a vicious cult. Still not comfortable with being touched, can their relationship survive Banshees and betrayal? In classic Slayton style, not everyone is who they seem. Friends become enemies, enemies become allies, souls are stolen, and battles fought. Backwoods Banshee is a fast paced, heart breaking, and wonderful addition to the Adam Binder series. About the Author David R. Slayton (He/Him) grew up in Guthrie, Oklahoma, where finding fantasy novels was pretty challenging and finding ones with diverse characters was downright impossible. Now he lives in Denver and writes the books he always wanted to read. His debut, White Trash Warlock , received a starred review from Publishers Weekly. In 2015, David founded Trick or Read , an initiative to give out books along with candy to children on Halloween as well as uplift lesser-known authors or those from marginalized backgrounds. His epic fantasy, Dark Moon, Shallow Sea , won the 2024 Colorado Book Award. Find him online at www.DavidRSlayton.com.

events.title: An Evening with Author Dan Wake
events.description: Join us for a conversation, Q&A, and book signing with author Dan Wake. Dan will be talking about his new travel memoir Eat the Wind: Travels with Dictators, Mercenaries, and Queens . About the Book After graduating from Stanford, Dan Wake was on track for a lucrative partnership at a big Washington law firm until he gave it all up to put adventure over career in 1985. It wasn’ t the first time he’ d rolled the dice to explore the world. From hitchhiking in freewheeling Europe to riding buses through the Amazon jungle to roaming through Asia in the shadow of dictatorship, Wake embraced the unpredictability of the open road and developed a Forrest Gump-like knack for dropping into events making world headlines. Whether he is charming his way through a royal jubilee in London, criss-crossing the Philippines during a bloody revolution, or simply finding remarkable people in remote places, Wake uses high adventure and keen humor to unveil the magic of unscripted travel before the internet changed the world. Eat the Wind vividly brings that enchantment alive and shows how it seduced a lifelong overachiever to risk his career for a chance to take the journey of a lifetime.

events.title: Storytime with 9-year-old author Clay Vilhauer
events.description: Join us for a special storytime with young author, Clay Vilhauer, and his mother, Amber Vilhauer, as they read the picture book What Nature Teaches Us: A Book About Being the Light . This is a free all ages event! About the Book: Designed for ages 5–12 and family read-alouds, the book uses lessons from the natural world, including the sun, river, mountain, cloud, and Colorado's state flower, the Columbine, to help children explore resilience, belonging, hope, and life's big emotions. It also includes a built-in "Your Turn" activity that encourages readers to head outdoors, making it a natural fit for story times, SEL programming, and family engagement events. About the Author: Clay Vilhauer is nine years old and already a bestselling author. At six, he announced he wanted to write a book -- six months later, The Long Forest Trail hit #1 on Amazon, won three awards, and reached more than 15,000 families. What Nature Teaches Us is his second book. He lives in Northern Colorado, goes outside as much as possible, and believes that when you focus on your thoughts and feelings, you can make the world a happier place. Amber Vilhauer is the founder of NGNG Enterprises -- No Guts, No Glory -- where she has spent twenty years helping impact-driven leaders bring their authentic voices into the world. She and Clay wrote What Nature Teaches Us in the pockets of a full life, going outside, paying attention, and appreciating each other as much as the world around them.

events.title: Meet Stephen Graham Jones, Author of ‘The Buffalo Hunter Hunter’
events.description: REGISTRATION REQUIRED - CLICK HERE Join New York Times bestselling author Stephen Graham Jones for an unforgettable evening exploring the art of horror, storytelling and writing. Jones will discuss his newest release, Off the Reservation , a sequel to the 2020 bestseller The Only Good Indians , along with the inspiration behind his chilling novels, creative process and how his Blackfeet heritage influences his work. Whether you are a devoted horror fan, an aspiring writer or simply enjoy meeting acclaimed authors, this is an event you won't want to miss! Based in Boulder, Stephen Graham Jones serves as the Ivena Baldwin Professor of English at the University of Colorado Boulder. Please note: This event is offsite at Embassy Suites DTC. Registration is required for this event through Arapahoe Libraries. REGISTER HERE
